PerfectoidQuotients.summary: Nothing prismatic exists in the pinned baseline: `prism`, `δ-ring`, `p-derivation`, `quasisyntomic`, `semiperfectoid`, `perfectoidization` and `Nygaard` all have zero hits in Mathlib's 246k and Tau Ceti's 71k declarations, and neither library even defines a perfectoid ring. What the libraries do supply is the integral prefix of Q0: Mathlib's Witt vectors (Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller, ghost components, truncation) together with `Perfection`/`PreTilt`, the multiplicative untilt, `WittVector.fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R` for any p-adically complete R and its surjectivity when Frobenius is surjective on R/p — so A_inf = W(R♭) and θ are available, in greater generality than BS22 assumes, all sorry-free. Also available as generic input: ordinary adic completion, flatness and faithfully flat descent for modules, regular sequences, divided power structures and the two-term cotangent complex. Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap actually plans: the principal generator of ker θ, derived p-adic completion, animated/simplicial commutative rings, δ-rings and prisms, prismatic cohomology and the Hodge–Tate comparison, universal prisms and perfectoidization, André's flatness lemma and the closed-quotient theorem 7.4/5.8.

targets.target: Integral perfectoid ring in the BS22 sense (p-adically complete, Frobenius surjective on R/p, kernel of θ principal)
targets.note: Neither library defines a perfectoid ring: `grep -rni perfectoid` over both trees returns only Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean and the three files of Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/, and none of them introduces a predicate. Mathlib works instead with the separate hypotheses `[IsAdicComplete (span {(p:R)}) R]` and `Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R p) p)`, and its own TODO in BDeRham.lean records that `ker θ` principal for integral perfectoid rings is not yet proved.

targets.target: Comparison of integral perfectoid rings with perfectoid Tate rings, and the integral subrings R°, R⁺
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Tate rings and the power-bounded subring A° (with A°° an ideal of it), so the integral-subring vocabulary exists, but there is no perfectoid Tate ring and hence no comparison; `IsUniform`/`IsStablyUniform` do not exist in either tree.

targets.target: A_inf = W(R♭) with θ : A_inf → R and its explicit description
targets.note: Mathlib builds R♭ = `PreTilt R p` = Perfection(R/p), the multiplicative untilt (sharp) map and `fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R` for any p-adically complete R, with surjectivity under Frobenius surjectivity on R/p — more general than BS22's hypothesis. Missing: the principal non-zero-divisor generator of ker θ, the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology on A_inf, and the residue map to W(k).

targets.target: Ordinary, derived p-adic and pseudouniformizer-adic completions kept separate
targets.note: Ordinary I-adic completion (`AdicCompletion`, `IsAdicComplete`) and the topological completion of a Huber ring exist; derived (p-complete) completion of a module or ring does not — `IsDerivedComplete`/`derivedCompletion` have no hits in either tree.

targets.target: Comparison lemmas for passing from a semiperfectoid quotient to a Tate ring
targets.note: `semiperfect` matches only `TauCeti.IsSemiperfectRing` (a Jacobson-radical notion in TauCeti/RingTheory/Jacobson/Semiperfect.lean, unrelated), and `semiperfectoid` has zero hits in both trees.

duplicates.note: PR.0 also asks for the equivalence between perfect prisms and integral perfectoid rings 'using the existing integral perfectoid/tilt/A_inf construction', i.e. exactly this prefix.
AI.0's integral prefix builds A_inf = W(O_C^♭), Frobenius and θ with its kernel generator, the same A_inf/θ package specialised to O_C.
F4 uses 'Q0's integral perfectoid criteria' for period annuli and restates the primitive kernel of θ as a Cartier divisor.

targets.target: δ-rings (p-derivations), free δ-algebras and Frobenius lifts
targets.note: `delta-ring`, `δ-ring` and `p-derivation` have zero hits in both trees. Mathlib has Witt-vector Frobenius and the Teichmüller lift, which is the comparison material the layer asks for, but no δ-structure.

targets.target: Distinguished elements, prisms, boundedness, morphisms of prisms, orientations, completed perfection
targets.note: `prism` has zero hits as a substring anywhere in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (216 008 + 70 802 declarations), so none of these notions exists.

targets.target: Correspondence between perfect prisms and integral perfectoid rings; the perfection theorem BS22 3.9
targets.note: Only the perfection functor itself (`Perfection`, `PerfectionMap`, `PreTilt`) is available; there is no prism side of the correspondence.

targets.target: Flatness and completion properties of prisms and their envelopes, with regular-sequence and torsion hypotheses
targets.note: Generic flatness and regular-sequence API is in Mathlib, but there is no prismatic or divided-power envelope in either tree (`envelope` matches only Karoubi/convex/injective-envelope files).

targets.target: Existing Witt-vector constructions, with every Frobenius lift compared to them
targets.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/ has 20 files: Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmüller, ghost components, truncated Witt vectors, the DVR structure for a perfect field and F-isocrystals, all sorry-free. This is the one target of the layer the libraries already supply.

targets.target: Simplicial commutative rings / animated rings and commutative algebra objects in a derived ∞-category, with their comparison
targets.note: `simplicial commutative ring`, `Animated` and `AnimatedRing` have zero hits; Mathlib has `SimplicialObject` in a general category but no simplicial commutative algebra, no ∞-categorical commutative algebra objects and so no comparison theorem in characteristic p.

targets.target: Cotangent, derived exterior-power and completion interfaces (DD.0–1)
targets.note: Mathlib has the two-term cotangent complex of an algebra extension with H^1 and base change, and Kähler differentials, but not the full simplicial cotangent complex L_{B/A} nor derived symmetric/exterior/divided powers (`derived exterior` has zero hits).

duplicates.note: The layer text says it imports PR.0's δ-rings, free δ-algebras, distinguished elements, prisms, orientations, completed perfection and the perfect-prism correspondence; PR.0 is the constructing owner.
E5 is the named owner of the simplicial/animated commutative algebra this layer imports.
DD.0 owns the cotangent complex and the derived exterior/symmetric power functors named here.

targets.target: Integral perfectoid rings in BS22's scope, and their relation to Tate perfectoid rings and integral subrings
targets.note: No perfectoid ring predicate exists in either library; Tau Ceti supplies Tate rings and pseudouniformizers but nothing perfectoid.

targets.target: A_inf/θ descriptions and the separation of the three completions
targets.note: Mathlib's `fontaineTheta` and `PreTilt` give A_inf = W(R♭) → R with surjectivity; only ordinary adic completion exists, derived p-completion does not.

targets.target: δ-rings, prisms, orientations, completed perfection and the perfect-prism/integral-perfectoid correspondence (imported from PR.0)
targets.note: Zero hits for `prism`/`δ-ring` in both trees.

targets.target: Witt-vector constructions and comparison of Frobenius lifts
targets.note: Complete and sorry-free in Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/.

targets.target: Simplicial commutative algebra and the cotangent/derived-exterior-power/completion interfaces
targets.note: Two-term cotangent complex and ordinary adic completion only; no animated rings, no derived powers, no derived completion.

duplicates.note: The roadmap summary states Q0's prism suffix now imports PR.0, which is the canonical owner of δ-rings, prisms and envelopes.
AI.0 reuses 'the common integral perfectoid ring and Witt-vector definitions' to build A_inf and θ; the same integral prefix.
P1 builds perfectoid Tate rings, R♭ and θ on the Tate side, which Q0 compares with its integral notion.

targets.target: Relative prismatic site of a p-completely smooth algebra over a bounded prism, with structure sheaf and flat coverings
targets.note: No prisms and no prismatic site in either tree; `prismatic` has zero hits.

targets.target: Čech–Alexander envelope models and their cohomology, independence of presentation, Frobenius functoriality
targets.note: Only the generic Čech nerve and Čech complex of a cover exist; there is no Čech–Alexander construction because there are no prismatic envelopes.

targets.target: Prismatic and divided-power (CR.0) envelopes and their flatness properties
targets.note: Mathlib has divided power structures, sub-PD-ideals, PD morphisms and the divided power algebra, but no PD envelope of an ideal and no flatness theorem for one.

targets.target: Crystalline and de Rham comparison in the cases used, with polynomial-coordinate calculations
targets.note: `crystalline` occurs in Mathlib only in Berthelot–Ogus bibliography entries of the DividedPowers files; there is no crystalline site, no de Rham complex of a ring map and no algebraic de Rham cohomology in either tree.

targets.target: BS22 Theorem 6.3 Hodge–Tate comparison with its multiplicative map and Breuil–Kisin twists
targets.note: `Hodge-Tate` matches only TauCeti's classical Tate Hodge structure ℤ(m) (TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Tate/Basic.lean), a different object; `Breuil` has zero hits.

targets.target: Gluing and base-change compatibility of the relative theory
targets.note: Nothing to glue: the underlying functor does not exist.

duplicates.note: The layer opens 'This is the named Q1 reexport of PR.1, not a second construction' — PR.1 owns the relative site, Čech–Alexander models and the Hodge–Tate comparison.
CR.0 owns the PD envelopes and their universal properties that this layer imports.
CR.2 owns the PD Poincaré lemma and the de Rham computations used for the crystalline comparison.
CP.1 assembles the same integral derived comparison diagram including the Hodge–Tate comparison.

targets.target: Universal prisms of semiperfectoid rings by adjoining, torsion removal and transfinite completion (BS22 7.2)
targets.note: No prisms exist, so no universal prism; `semiperfectoid` has zero hits.

targets.target: Universal perfectoidization (BS22 7.3) with its universal property
targets.note: `perfectoidization` has zero hits in either tree.

targets.target: Coherent left Kan extension of the prismatic functor to derived p-complete simplicial commutative algebras (Construction 7.6)
targets.note: Mathlib has left Kan extensions of ordinary functors, but no animated rings and no derived p-completion, so the construction cannot even be stated.

targets.target: Filtered derived Hodge–Tate comparison with graded pieces given by completed derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex
targets.note: Only the two-term cotangent complex of an extension exists; derived exterior powers and the filtration are absent.

targets.target: Base-change, colimit and descent properties of the derived functor
targets.note: Depends on the absent functor.

targets.target: Discreteness/δ-structure and initial-object statements 7.7–7.10, the idempotent-retract lemma, the regular-quotient calculation and the quasiregular semiperfectoid case
targets.note: Idempotents and retracts exist generically; none of these prismatic statements does.

targets.target: Flat base change compatibility needed to descend surjectivity of perfectoidization
targets.note: Generic flatness/faithful flatness only.

duplicates.note: The layer explicitly imports PR.2's left Kan extension, filtered Hodge–Tate comparison and 7.7–7.10 statements; PR.2 is the owner.
DD.0 owns the cotangent complex and derived exterior powers whose completed versions give the graded pieces here.

targets.target: Quasisyntomic and quasiregular semiperfectoid conditions with their cotangent criteria (imported from DD.0/DD.5)
targets.note: `quasisyntomic` has zero hits in both trees; only the two-term cotangent complex exists, and the mod-p amplitude condition that defines the class is not formulated.

targets.target: Lifting theorem for quasisyntomic covers to bounded prisms (BS22 7.11)
targets.note: No prisms, no quasisyntomic covers.

targets.target: Preservation of faithful flatness under completed perfection
targets.note: Mathlib has faithfully flat modules and faithfully flat descent for modules, and the perfection functor, but no statement relating them, and no completed perfection.

targets.target: BS22 Theorem 7.14 (André): every integral perfectoid ring has a p-completely faithfully flat perfectoid extension that is absolutely integrally closed
targets.note: `absolutely integrally closed` has zero hits; only ordinary integral closedness is available. André's flatness lemma is not in either library.

targets.target: Construction by adjoining roots of monic polynomials, lifting, perfecting and transfinite iteration, with completeness/perfectoidness/faithful flatness/size bounds at limit stages
targets.note: `AdjoinRoot` for a single polynomial exists; the transfinite construction and its limit-stage estimates do not.

targets.target: Compatible p-power roots of a specified element
targets.note: An element of `Perfection R p` is exactly a compatible system of p-power roots, so the bookkeeping notion exists in characteristic p; the mixed-characteristic statement that such a system can be adjoined to an integral perfectoid ring does not.

targets.target: The auxiliary refinements BS22 7.12–7.15
targets.note: Absent with the rest of the prismatic material.

duplicates.note: DD.5 owns the quasisyntomic site and the elementary compatible-root semiperfectoid covers, and explicitly disclaims Q3's stronger absolutely-integrally-closed theorem.
DD.0 defines quasisyntomic maps by p-complete flatness and the mod-p cotangent amplitude condition imported here.
PR.2 supplies the discreteness calculation for quasiregular semiperfectoid inputs that this stage's construction uses.

targets.target: BS22 Theorem 7.4: surjectivity of perfectoidization for a semiperfectoid quotient
targets.note: Perfectoidization does not exist in either library.

targets.target: Reduction of the ideal to finitely many generators by a completed filtered colimit, then to a principal ideal
targets.note: Generic finite-generation and filtered-colimit API exists; the completed version of the argument does not.

targets.target: Identification of perfectoidization with the completed quotient by all p-power roots of the generator, and its descent
targets.note: No perfectoidization; nothing to identify.

targets.target: Remark 7.5: for a perfectoid Tate ring R with plus ring R⁺ and an ideal defining a Zariski closed subset, the semiperfectoid completed integral quotient, its perfectoidization and inversion of the pseudouniformizer
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Huber pairs (A,A⁺) and Wedhorn 7.38: the quotient Huber pair induces a closed embedding of adic spectra whose range is the locus of points whose support contains the ideal. That is the topological shadow of the statement; the perfectoid content (completed integral quotient, perfectoidization, inverting ϖ) is absent.

targets.target: Universal property, surjectivity from R, identification of the plus ring as an integral closure, almost surjectivity on integral rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti knows that replacing the plus ring by its integral closure leaves Spa unchanged, but there is no almost mathematics in either tree, so 'almost surjectivity' cannot be stated.

targets.target: The resulting spectrum is the prescribed Zariski closed subset (ECD Theorem 5.8)
targets.note: No perfectoid spaces, hence no Zariski closed perfectoid subspaces.

duplicates.note: P4 owns the elementary §5 morphism theory and states that the stronger 'Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed' (ECD 5.8) is supplied by Q4; the two layers share the closed-immersion carriers.
P8 combines a tower's closed loci with 'Q4's universal perfectoidization' and controls the same plus ring and integral almost surjection.
S2 depends on Q4 for the normalized/perfectoidized local models of a Hodge-type embedding.
S4 also depends on Q4 for the closed-locus perfectoidization inside the Hansen–Johansson descent.
